title: Priority scoring matrix for enterprise console exports and cost views
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit many non-bug console requests for exports, custom cost breakdowns, and dashboard slices. Intake is ad hoc, engineering effort gets misprioritized, and customers experience long lead times for seemingly similar asks. Goal: Define a repeatable intake + triage flow and a lightweight priority scoring matrix tailored for console/reporting requests so product can reliably grade requests, provide clear SLAs, and route high-impact work to Dedicated/Private roadmap or short-term tactical mocks.

Scope: This ticket covers the product-side definition and runbook for triaging incoming console/reporting requests (usage analytics, export formats, cost breakdowns, custom dashboards). It does NOT include implementation PRs or infra changes; it should deliver a scoring rubric, intake form template, SLA tiers, and a handoff checklist for engineering and solutions teams.

Out-of-scope: Non-console telemetry requests, incident responses, and low-level billing infra refactors (those will be captured as dependent ENG work).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented scoring matrix (CSV-friendly) that maps request attributes to priority score (customer size, revenue profile, security constraints, SLA need, dev effort estimate, strategic alignment).
2) An intake form (Confluence + short link) and template that CS/Solutions/AMs can use.
3) SLAs and routing rules for three tiers (Fast-track <2w, Standard 2-8w, Roadmap >8w).
4) A handoff checklist for ENG with required artifacts (sample dataset, expected schema, privacy constraints, mock dashboard image).
5) 3 pilot requests triaged using the matrix with documented outcomes and one retrospective decision log.
notes: Design trade-off: keep scoring lean (<=10 fields) to ensure adoption by CS; computeable fields preferred to minimize guesswork.

We will align severity with customer commitment: e.g., Dedicated contracts + >=$50k ARR get +2 priority bias; security/compliance narrow use cases may bump requests to Roadmap with engineering pre-review.

Suggested scoring buckets: Customer Impact (0-5), Business Fit (0-3), Implementation Complexity (0-5 inverted), Data Sensitivity (0-2), Repeatability (0-2), SLA Urgency (0-3). Final score normalized to 0-20.
Early implementation should expose raw scoring attributes as columns in the ticket to enable dashboards and retro analytics.

implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): finalize scoring matrix, publish intake form, train CS/Solutions on usage. Phase 2 (4 weeks): pilot 3 customer requests, collect feedback, refine rubric. Phase 3 (iterative): integrate scoring attributes into ticketing labels and dashboard; propose minor console UX affordances for request status and expected SLA visibility.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: CS may not adopt a new intake form. Mitigation: keep form <=6 fields and embed in existing CS workflow (Slack + Zendesk templates).
Risk: Matrix misclassifies requests causing engineering churn. Mitigation: require an ENG pre-review step for scores above threshold and collect retrospective data to recalibrate weights.
outcomes_and_metrics: Adoption: >=80% of new console/reporting requests go through intake form within 6 weeks. SLA compliance: 90% of Fast-track requests delivered or properly scoped within 2 weeks. Predictability: reduce average lead time for prioritized requests by 30% vs baseline. Visibility: dashboard showing weekly distribution of request scores and time-to-delivery per tier.
